text.p: Canadian gold group Barrick Gold Corp was expected to launch a full takeover bid for Joe Gutnick's Great Central Mines Ltd within days, The Australian Financial Review newspaper said on Wednesday.
"Barrick is known to have had a team of executives in Australia casting their eyes over the Great Central assets," the Financial Review said in its Chanticleer column.
Great Central's share price has risen from a A$2.10 low last week to its A$2.46 close on Tuesday because of takeover speculation, the newspaper said.
Tuesday's closing level values Great Central at about A$625 million.
Any takeover bid would value Great Central at closer to A$700 million, the newspaper said.
Gutnick was not immediately available for comment but told The Melbourne Age newspaper that he had received a number of offers, without elaborating.

Great Central Mines posted net profits for the six months to December 31 of A$15.56 million on sales of A$128.75 million and gold production of 236,469 ounces at an average cash cost of A$255 an ounce.
Great Central's current resource estimate stands at 6.3 million ounces of gold while proved and probable reserves stand at 2.6 million ounces.
